lab_ocr_unavailable.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3: an OCR evaluation of actinglab or the Lab cannot run because the offline tool loaded no usable OCR model. The offline tools load the OCR provider the Runtime uses (the in-process ppocr-ctc engine over the model folders of the vision root that the Runtime configuration's vision section names, always on the CPU). A command that would evaluate an OCR target refuses with this code (exit 3) and names the target as target_id; a Lab mark self-test, the first decision of record stop and the capabilities report give it as their reason. path is the vision root when it is known. Its caused_by link says why: lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured, a configuration read or decode code, vision_root_unavailable, vision_models_empty, lab_ocr_model_missing or lab_ocr_runtime_missing.
lab_ocr_unavailable.common_causes: actinglab runs outside an installation or a single-location root, the configuration has no vision section, or the vision root holds no OCR model folder.
lab_ocr_unavailable.handling: Install the OCR model folder and ONNX Runtime under the Runtime's vision root and run actinglab from the installation's tools (or runtime) folder.

lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3, a cause of lab_ocr_unavailable: the offline tool has no Runtime configuration with a vision section. It does not run from an installation or a single-location root, or the selected configuration has no vision section.
lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured.common_causes: actinglab was started from a copy outside the installation, or the Runtime configuration has no vision section.
lab_ocr_vision_unconfigured.handling: Run actinglab from the installation's tools folder, or add the vision section to the Runtime configuration.

lab_ocr_model_missing.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3, a cause of lab_ocr_unavailable: the vision root's models folder (path) holds model folders, but none is an OCR model.

lab_ocr_runtime_missing.description: Workflow #396 LAB-3, a cause of lab_ocr_unavailable: the vision root has no usable ONNX Runtime library at path (ort\onnxruntime.dll). Its caused_by link is the OS failure when the OS reported one.

record_click_follow_invalid.description: Workflow #396 REC-4: a click of a Lab recording step that follows a template mark (record mark --click-follow, a request's click.follow) does not hold; mark_id is the followed mark and follow_problem says why. A declaration that cannot hold (not_template, not_required, guard_conflict) refuses record mark with this code (exit 3) and nothing is written. A frame of the step on which the click does not hold (primary_mismatch on the primary frame, template_unmatched or click_outside_frame on any live frame) is a refused mark's reason inside record_mark_rejected, with the frame. The stage is record_click_follow_check.
record_click_follow_invalid.common_causes: The click follows a color, OCR or check mark, a template that only an any_of check names, or another guard was named; the template matches elsewhere on the primary frame, is not found on a sample frame, or the followed click box leaves a sample frame.
record_click_follow_invalid.handling: Follow a required template mark of the step and let it be the guard; crop the template so that its best match on the primary frame is the crop itself; give it a search area that covers every position it moves to, and a click box that stays inside the frame there.

record_gesture_execution_unsupported.description: #411 Lab BD: do --capture --record was asked to execute a Lab recording step whose declared gesture a Lab operation cannot press, a single-touch drag with a vertical brake (single_touch_drag_with_vertical_brake_v1); nothing was captured, pressed or recorded (exit 3).
record_gesture_execution_unsupported.common_causes: The open step declares a brake drag; Lab operations press taps, long taps and swipes only, and running one declared operation as the kernel runs it is not available in this version.
record_gesture_execution_unsupported.handling: Reach the screen after the gesture by other means (for example a lab run of a package that performs it), then close the step with record mark --close-step or give its next frame offline; the generated package still declares the gesture.

record_click_follow_check.description: Checking a Lab recording click that follows a template mark: its declaration, and the followed template and its click box on every live frame of the step (Workflow #396 REC-4).
